proves.claim: Exact redundant C(P,Q) on a later fetched B uses the ordinary already receipt without merging, checking, deriving or pushing.

landing.job.redundant-checked-already.why: A checked synthetic descendant can add no tree change even though it is absent from trunk history.

proves.claim: Changed trees, uncontained source or first parent, reversed and non-two-parent heads remain pending and obey the ordinary check.

landing.job.redundant-checked-exclusions.why: Equal trees or source containment alone must never discard a real reviewed resolution or unlanded first parent.

proves.claim: A redundant checked head is already while a real sibling still checks and lands normally.

landing.job.redundant-checked-mixed.why: Metadata-only recognition must not swallow a real sibling or skip its landing checks.

proves.claim: A redundant checked Sprint head still reaches its check and exact-tree proof, and a red proof cannot move trunk.

landing.job.redundant-checked-sprint-exc.why: The steady recovery must not weaken Sprint exact-tree proof or its red no-push limit.

proves.claim: Missing, malformed and non-commit objects and Git failures never establish redundant containment.

landing.job.redundant-checked-invalid-ob.why: Missing objects, grafted history and Git errors must fail closed rather than count as containment.

proves.claim: Replacement refs and inherited selectors cannot change the immutable redundant-merge decision.

landing.job.redundant-checked-object-ide.why: Replacement refs and inherited Git selectors must not substitute objects for the accepted checked head.

proves.claim: A redundant shape never skips the native fetched-ref identity check.

landing.job.redundant-checked-ref-moved.why: Object classification must remain behind the native fetched-ref identity guard.
